title: k8s-node-provisioning-debug-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Sporadic node provisioning failures during cluster autoscale tests on dev/staging clusters (aws-us-west-2).
- Symptoms: nodes created by ASG/Cluster Autoscaler enter NotReady or remain in Provisioning state for >10m, kubelet fails to register.
- Repro window: 2026-02-26 -> 2026-02-28 during spike tests.

Objective:
- Capture commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses and next steps so we can reproduce and hand off to SRE if needed.

Chronology / Breadcrumbs:
2026-02-26 09:12 - first alert (RD-3120)
- Cluster autoscaler scaled up 3 nodes, all stayed NotReady.

Commands tried (local kubeconfig pointed at staging cluster):
1) kubectl get nodes -o wide
Output snippet: 
NAME                                        STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION
n-aws-stg-20260226-1   NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.27.3   10.0.24.57    <none>        Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS   5.15.0-88-generic

2) kubectl describe node n-aws-stg-20260226-1
Looked for: Conditions, Events, Kubelet start logs in Events.
Events showed repeated: 
  Warning  NodeNotReady  2m (x10 over 3m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-24-57  Node n-aws-stg-20260226-1 status is now: NodeNotReady

3) kubectl logs -n kube-system daemonset/aws-node -l k8s-app=aws-node --tail=200 (check CNI)
- aws-node logs looked fine, no obvious ENI/double-attach errors.

4) ssh into instance (via bastion): sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,300p'
Key snippets: 
Feb 26 09:15:24 ip-10-0-24-57 kubelet[1234]: E0226 09:15:24.123456  1234 kubelet.go:2263] Container runtime network not ready: NetworkReady=false reason:NetworkPluginNotReady message:docker: network plugin returns error: cni failed to set up pod "pause-...": failed to write netconf: open /etc/cni/net.d/10-aws.conflist: no such file or directory
Feb 26 09:16:00 ip-10-0-24-57 kubelet[1234]: E0226 09:16:00.789012  1234 kubelet_node_status.go:384] Failed to update node status: Post "https://10.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/nodes/n-aws-stg-20260226-1/status": dial tcp 10.0.0.1:6443: i/o timeout

Hypothesis 1: CNI plugin config not present/installed on provisioning image or race condition where kubelet starts before CNI config is written by bootstrap systemd unit.
Hypothesis 2: Networking from node to control plane intermittently blocked (security groups or eni not attached correctly) causing kubelet to fail updating status.
Hypothesis 3: Cloud-init/packer image drift - new AMI missing some init scripts that create /etc/cni/net.d/ files.

What I tried (attempts to fix / validate):
A) sudo ls -la /etc/cni/net.d -> returned empty or missing 10-aws.conflist on affected nodes.
B) systemctl status aws-cni-setup.service (custom unit we use in image to populate cni conf) -> showed failed with exit code 1 in some instances; logs indicate retry loop for attaching eni metadata.
C) Re-run unit: sudo systemctl restart aws-cni-setup.service && journalctl -u aws-cni-setup -n 200 --no-pager
- After manual restart, unit created /etc/cni/net.d/10-aws.conflist and kubelet transitioned to Ready after ~20s. (manual fix success)
D) Compare a healthy node vs unhealthy node filesystem (tar list): healthy nodes have /opt/cni/bin/aws-cni and conflist present. Unhealthy nodes missing /opt/cni/bin/aws-cni sometimes.
E) kubectl get pod -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-proxy -o wide -> kube-proxy crashloops on nodes missing CNI.

Errors captured (raw snippets):
- "failed to write netconf: open /etc/cni/net.d/10-aws.conflist: no such file or directory"
- "dial tcp 10.0.0.1:6443: i/o timeout"
- "systemd: aws-cni-setup.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE"

Additional checks done:
- Verified AMI build logs in artifact storage (s3://redwood-ami-builds/staging/2026-02-20/) - image build shows aws-cni binary packaged, but the systemd unit expects metadata from IMDS v2 which our bootstrap script occasionally times out waiting for a token.
- Tested IMDS token retrieval locally: curl -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60" -> sometimes 403 in terraform-created spot instances during scale-up (suspect EBS-backed launch config timing).

Quick repro commands for SRE handoff:
1) Launch a test instance using the staging AMI and same launch template used by ASG.
2) SSH and run: sudo systemctl restart aws-cni-setup.service; sudo journalctl -u aws-cni-setup -n 200
3) Check presence: ls -la /etc/cni/net.d; ls -la /opt/cni/bin
4) kubectl describe node <name> and watch events.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Added a post-launch hook to ASG (bootstrap script) to retry IMDS token fetch up to 5 times with backoff. Deployed to staging launch template (lt-stg-v8).
- Bumped health-check timeout in cluster-autoscaler to 8m to reduce noisy evictions while nodes finishing bootstrap.

Follow-ups / Next steps:
- [ ] Add more robust IMDS v2 token retry logic in packer image (or fallback to IMDSv1 for bootstrap path) and rebuild AMI.
- [ ] Add unit test in image build pipeline to assert /etc/cni/net.d/10-aws.conflist exists.
- [ ] Run smoke tests after AMI update: spin up 50 nodes in staging pool and ensure >95% come Ready within 3m.
- [ ] Have SRE validate security group / routing for control plane reachability during scale-up.
- [ ] Postmortem notes for RD-3120 with timeline and manual fixes performed.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could be worth instrumenting aws-cni-setup.service to emit metrics to CloudWatch (success/fail counts per instance) so we can detect regression earlier.
- Consider switching to a node-init container approach (DaemonSet) that runs once and writes CNI files after instance is up; more resilient to AMI drift.

Hand-off summary for SRE/Infra team:
- Problem: Missing CNI config on newly provisioned nodes causing kubelet network plugin error and NodeNotReady. Manual restart of aws-cni-setup.service fixes the node.
- Likely root cause: IMDS token retrieval race/timeouts during bootstrap causing systemd unit to fail to write conflist.
- Temporary mitigations: increased CA health timeout, launch-template script updated to retry IMDS.
- Permanant fix proposal: AMI rebuild with improved bootstrap resilience + CI check + consider daemonset-based bootstrap.

Attachments / links:
- JIRA RD-3120: incident ticket with alerts and pager timeline.
- AMI build logs: s3://redwood-ami-builds/staging/2026-02-20/
- Slack thread: #infra-auto-provision (see pinned messages)

---- END SCRATCHPAD ----
summary: Personal scratchpad capturing commands, errors, hypotheses and manual fixes for sporadic node provisioning failures where CNI config was missing; manual restart of aws-cni-setup.service remedied nodes. Next: AMI rebuild and CI check.
